Florian Wirtz helping to unlock Alexander Isak at Liverpool as Antonio Silva shines for Bournemouth - The Radar
Alexander Isak added two more goals to his tally against Club Brugge and earned praise for his all-round play, so what's behind the Liverpool striker's return to form? Plus, the Bournemouth summer signing already providing value for money under Marco Rose
Thursday 26 November 2026 15:56, UK
Welcome to The Radar, a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:
🔺Secrets behind Isak's return to form
🔺Bournemouth's next defensive gem
🔺A player to watch this weekend
Isak's Wirtz connection and left-foot finishing
Alexander Isak reached double figures for the season with his two goals in Liverpool's 3-0 victory over Club Brugge. His finishes, a first-time effort from a cut-back and a dink over the goalkeeper in a one-on-one, showed he is playing with confidence again.

The 27-year-old is swiftly putting an injury-hit first season at Liverpool behind him. He faces Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday having become only the eighth player in the club's history to score in six consecutive away games in all competitions.
Andoni Iraola praised the quality of his link-up play after the game against Club Brugge. His total of 44 touches was his highest in any fixture this season and came three days after he recorded his next-highest total with 39 in the 4-0 win over Manchester United.
The numbers are encouraging for Iraola as he tries to bring cohesion to his attack. He wants Isak to be involved in Liverpool's approach play. But the striker is benefitting from spending more time where is most dangerous too: in the opposition penalty area.
His box touches per 90 minutes have leapt by 60 per cent in the Premier League this season. He is also averaging 53 per cent more shots. But the increase has been most dramatic in his numbers for goals and expected goals, both of which have doubled.
Isak is scoring more because he is getting better-quality chances. And Florian Wirtz, another expensive signing who struggled last term, has played a vital role in improving the striker's service.
Wednesday's game provided more evidence of the understanding developing between the two players. According to Opta, Wirtz found Isak with 10 passes, nearly twice as many as anyone else.
Wirtz also made more passes to Isak than any team-mate on Sunday against Manchester United, with six, including one from which Isak nearly scored in the 75th minute. In the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace, there was a cute pass to set up his goal.
Going further back, it was Wirtz who played Isak in behind for the cut-back which led to Liverpool's penalty against Brentford. Against Brighton and Nottingham Forest, there were passes over the top which would have put Isak through if not for loose touches.
In total in the Premier League, Wirtz has made 29 passes to Isak - 10 more than anyone else. He is finding Isak at a rate of 3.35 times per 90 minutes, up from 2.57 times per 90 minutes last season.
Data from Gradient Sports highlights that he is providing quality as well as quantity with his passes. Wirtz ranks behind only Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard in the Premier League this season for passes into a dangerous position, with 62.
Of course, the relationship between a striker and his No 10 has to work both ways. And Isak, fitter and sharper than at any point in his Liverpool career following an uninterrupted pre-season, is certainly doing his bit when it comes to his movement.
According to Opta, he ranks top among all Premier League players this season for runs in behind, runs ending in the opposition box and runs making him an option for a cross. He is also top for runs followed by team shots and team goals.
The volume and quality of Isak's runs is making Wirtz's task easier when it comes to providing service. But importantly, Isak has also added variety and unpredictability to his finishing.
This season in the Premier League, he has scored four goals with his weaker left foot compared to three with his right. Eleven games in, it is already his highest total of left-footed goals in a season since arriving in the Premier League with Newcastle in 2022.
Gradient's data shows a sharp rise in his left-footed shooting. Isak has taken 37.9 per cent of his shots on his left this term, compared to roughly 15 per cent across the previous two seasons.
As with Wirtz's passes, it is a matter of quality as well as quantity.
Gradient's grading system, in which players are graded out of 100 in a wide range of categories based on the quality of their execution, shows Isak's left-footed shooting grade has improved across the last three seasons, from 60, to 70 to 75, meaning he has gone from the 46th percentile to the 94th in the space of two years.
The improvement has made him more difficult to defend against.
Consider his second goal against Ipswich in September, when both Dara O'Shea and Kjell Scherpen were anticipating a right-footed shot, only for Isak to shift the ball onto his left and score.
Brentford were similarly flummoxed by his goal at the Gtech Community Stadium in October, when he fired a left-footed finish through a crowd of bodies a split second after controlling Bradley Barcola's back-post knockdown using his right.
With Wirtz picking out his runs, with the goals flowing, and with growing trust in his weaker foot, Isak will feel confident of extending his scoring run in Sunday's Merseyside derby.
Huijsen, Zabarnyi… Silva?
Bournemouth face Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports+ on Sunday, having won a club-record 10 straight games while only conceding three goals. If there is one area which encapsulates this club's capacity to renew and rebuild, it is their defence.
Over the course of the last two summers, Bournemouth have lost five starting defenders in Dean Huijsen, Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez, Alex Jimenez and Marcos Senesi. An entire backline dismantled. And yet they have become defensively stronger this season.
Bournemouth rank among the Premier League's top four sides for expected goals against and shots allowed this season. Only Arsenal have allowed fewer shots on target.
Bournemouth's goals conceded column is skewed by their 5-1 loss to Chelsea in early October. But they haven't lost since. Their 10-game winning run has included seven clean sheets.
Alongside James Hill, Antonio Silva has played a big part. He already looks like one of the signings of the season following his £25.7m arrival from Benfica. Carry on as he has started and the club will be confident of one day banking another hefty profit.
For now, though, they can just enjoy the contribution of the latest centre-back to demonstrate elite quality for the club. Silva was no unknown. He joined as a Portugal international with 183 senior appearances for his boyhood club Benfica behind him.
But it still took shrewd judgement to know his qualities would transfer to the Premier League. And Bournemouth have demonstrated a handy knack for getting these things right.
In an interview with Sky Sports in August, Joao Nuno Fonseca, a former coach in the Benfica development team, highlighted the quality of Silva's anticipation and his ability to read the game, all of which has been evident since his arrival at Bournemouth.
Gradient Sports, whose analysts grade player actions by execution quality, give him a positioning grade of 86.7 out of 100 this term, putting him among the Premier League's best defenders. Only Jeremy Jacquet beats his 79.5 one-vs-one defending grade.
Silva has also shown his technical quality. Crucially for Marco Rose, who favours quick, vertical passes like Iraola, the 23-year-old is a forward-thinking passer. Only Jan Paul van Hecke has completed more line-breaking passes among centre-backs this season.
He is comfortable punching passes through midfield and is also able to switch the play with long diagonals. According to Gradient, he scores above his positional average in a wide-range of passing categories, demonstrating the extent of his offering on the ball.
After Huijsen and Zabarnyi, now at Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, Silva looks like the latest Bournemouth centre-back destined to reach the very top.
Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on
Quentin Timber, brother of Arsenal's Jurrien, is earning positive reviews at Crystal Palace. They've won five of the 12 games he has started this season and only one of the six he hasn't. It's Hull next for the Eagles, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.
Live Radar: What's on Sky this weekend?
Seven Premier League games are live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting when Nottingham Forest host Chelsea at 8pm on Friday.
Saturday sees Ipswich Town take on Aston Villa at 5.30pm.
There are five games live on Sunday, with Brighton hosting Newcastle, Crystal Palace facing Hull, Fulham taking on Bournemouth and Sunderland hosting Tottenham all at 2.05pm before Arsenal face Manchester City at 4.30pm.
